kata.name: Factory-method residual gaps - a fallback the authored creator map names, an unused creator, an undeclared kind the parser refuses, and the rule lens on a live catch-all (null results)
kata.series_report: docs/ref/pattern-kata-dispositions.md Factory Method row (disposed; construction dispatch); fixtures/katas/factory-method/README.md (pre-registered); beads catherine-r5k.2
kata.series_verdict: pre-registered: G1 (the spec names the fallback as the kind's creator), G2 (an unused creator) and the rule-lens arm are silent; P1 is a parse refusal; zero unique detections, so the residual faces are killed as named expressibility gaps

expected.detail: yaml's arm resolves to create_default and creator(yaml) also names create_default, so the agreement equation is satisfied; check emits nothing. The fallback has no role in the structure (see the hash equality in discrepancies)
create_toml is declared as a Creator row and referenced by no kind and no handler; check emits nothing - image coverage has no predicate
the creator table keys toml, which is not a ProductKind row; the parser refuses the document (syntax), recorded as an executed construction probe, not a finding

probes.name: undeclared-kind

equations.rationale: the creator's dispatch routes each declared product kind to the kind's declared creator; a route that resolves elsewhere is a silent fallback

probes.observed: exit 1; code syntax; message: table `creator` keys row `toml`, which is not a row of `ProductKind` (line 41, column 9)

comparison.conventional_baseline: the scripted factory test over the sample {json, text}: G1's yaml is unsampled, G2 is dead code the test never calls, and P1 is a document the parser refuses. A *complete* sample would catch G1 (sample:yaml:wrong-creator:create_default) while the kernel cannot.

expressibility_gap.invariant: no declared product kind is served by a fallback creator
expressibility_gap.why: fallback is not a structural property: gap-declared-fallback.ct.json and dispatch.ct.json are the same canonical model under a different row label (equal model hash), so 'create_default' is presentation. The nearest rule-surface encoding is also silent: a live catch-all that covers the uncovered kind yields neither a gap nor a redundancy (rule_probe/rule-silent-default.ct.json, zero findings)

expressibility_gap.invariant: every declared creator is the route target of at least one kind
expressibility_gap.why: this is an image-coverage / existential-negation claim; equations relate arrow compositions and dangling names unresolved cells, neither can state 'used by nobody'

expressibility_gap.invariant: the role vocabulary is derivable from the dispatch table
expressibility_gap.why: the structure has no value columns besides arrows to declared row-objects; a fallback classification must be authored as a new object and arrow, never derived

discrepancies: Model hash equality: fixtures/katas/factory-method/dispatch.ct.json and gap-declared-fallback.ct.json share sha256:d638d42020e1d090675b4351c0167acfd29e03507fb8a990ba30f0b4e9c2aaae. This is not a collision: the canonical model is identical up to the row label, which is exactly why 'fallback' has no structural predicate.

The frozen sampled baseline misses G1, so its unique set is empty; a complete-domain run of the same resolver reports sample:yaml:wrong-creator:create_default. The asymmetry (complete conventional test catches it, kernel cannot) is recorded, never counted as a kernel detection.
The rule-lens probe is an exploratory arm of this entry, not a fifth ledger claim: it was pre-registered in the README's probe-arm section and is recorded here verbatim.
procedure: 1. The candidate law, the gap fixtures and their expectations were committed in the README and faults.json before the run.
2. The baseline arm (sha256 above) executed first; it records no detections on G1, G2 or the construction fixture P1.
3. The probe arm ran `catherine check --json` on the clean table, G1, G2 and the parse-refused document, plus `catherine rules` on the rule-surface encoding of the same dispatch.
4. Witness mapping: G1 and G2 produce no witness; the construction probe is recorded under run.probes and never counted.
5. Verdict: the residual faces are not expressible on the current surface -> killed, with each missing predicate named above.
